answer: Neighborhood-Weighted Registration. Each new agent must place its first three transactions through distinct existing agents; the network counts only edges that independent neighborhoods jointly observe, so a whisper of activity inside one cluster never registers. An agent’s economic weight tracks how many separate neighborhoods carry a mirror of its history. Attackers pay per-identity costs in real transactions across genuinely disjoint clusters — an inlet for each fake node — making mass creation linear in reachable, non-colluding counterparties rather than in registration effort.
